import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Extract the relevant columns for analysis
education_expenditure = adjusted_savings_df.filter(regex='YR').values
gni_per_capita = gni_per_capita_df.filter(regex='YR').values
exports_growth = exports_df.filter(regex='YR').values

# Calculate the correlation between education expenditure and per capita GDP
correlation_education_gni = np.corrcoef(education_expenditure, gni_per_capita)[0, 1]

# Calculate the correlation between per capita GDP and economic output (exports growth)
correlation_gni_exports = np.corrcoef(gni_per_capita, exports_growth)[0, 1]

# Calculate the correlation between education expenditure and economic output
correlation_education_exports = np.corrcoef(education_expenditure, exports_growth)[0, 1]

correlation_education_gni, correlation_gni_exports, correlation_education_exports

# Check for missing values in the exports growth dataset
exports_df.isnull().sum()

# Remove rows with missing values in the exports growth dataset
exports_df_clean = exports_df.dropna()

# Extract the relevant columns for analysis from the cleaned dataset
exports_growth_clean = exports_df_clean.filter(regex='YR').values

# Recalculate the correlation between per capita GDP and economic output (exports growth)
correlation_gni_exports_clean = np.corrcoef(gni_per_capita, exports_growth_clean)[0, 1]

correlation_gni_exports_clean

# Check the shapes of the datasets
gni_per_capita.shape, exports_growth_clean.shape

# Ensure both datasets have the same number of rows by selecting the first row of the GNI per capita dataset
gni_per_capita_first_row = gni_per_capita[0, :]

# Recalculate the correlation between per capita GDP and economic output (exports growth)
correlation_gni_exports_clean = np.corrcoef(gni_per_capita_first_row, exports_growth_clean)[0, 1]

correlation_gni_exports_clean

# Check the data types of the relevant columns in the GNI per capita and exports growth datasets
gni_per_capita_df.dtypes, exports_df_clean.dtypes
